name: The rendering hardware is part of the job's identity
summary: The renderer choice (GPU vs software) is frozen onto the export plan at planning time, hashed into the plan fingerprint, and the sandbox's device grant is derived from that frozen record rather than from the worker's environment; afterwards the actual renderer identity is audited from a privileged vantage point the untrusted page cannot reach, failing closed on a silent software fallback.
insight: An environment capability is treated as a term in the work's identity, and the grant of that capability is derived FROM the identity rather than from the executing host; and the identity claim is verified by splitting the question into the part the subject may answer and the part only an outside observer may answer.
field: Headless browsers standardly render on the CPU for determinism; GPU passthrough is mature published practice; pinning environment inputs into a build hash is founding doctrine of hermetic build systems; verifying the toolchain afterwards is reproducible-build practice; reading page state from an isolated execution context is a documented automation capability.
case_against: Three known parts assembled. Consent link is incidental and conceded.
answer: The pin is the AUTHORITY at grant time, not a description of a decision made elsewhere; an operator with root on the worker can change which device is offered and cannot change whether it is taken. The isolated-world audit is the recognition that the obvious check reads the one field the failure's beneficiary controls.

name: Proving untrusted content renders with no network at all
summary: Customer-authored packages are statically parsed at publish time (tokeniser for markup, lexer for code); every external reference is graded by what its absence would cost the captured picture (boot / visual / cosmetic); boot-critical references are satisfied from pinned, hash-verified library packs shipped inside the server image and materialised into a DISPOSABLE capture copy whose dependency table is rewritten; visual-only references are spliced out of the copy; the stored package is never mutated; the verdict is three-valued and re-derived at export rather than read from a stored flag.
insight: Grading an external dependency by its effect on the captured pixels rather than by resource type, which is what makes a third 'compatible-with-substitutions' state shippable; and satisfying rather than rejecting, which makes the verdict relative to a mirror the platform maintains so adding a library is a data commit.
field: Vendoring dependencies and rewriting where they resolve from is established (mainstream framework tooling does exactly this); hermetic builds are founded on it; pinned versions with recorded hashes is standard supply-chain discipline; industries accepting third-party interactive bundles routinely validate self-containment and REJECT external references; severity grading is ordinary linter design.
case_against: Sandbox has no network, package needs a library, vendor it. Five-minute conclusion.
answer: The vendoring conclusion is conceded. The grading AXIS (consequence for pixels, cutting across resource type) is not what an engineer reaches for, and the never-mutate rule preserves an identity property other subsystems silently depend on.
caveat: The static scan does not cover CSS url(), img/video/audio src, workers or wasm. The runtime audit that two comments claim closes that gap is fully built with a named failure classification but is imported ONLY by a diagnostic script, not by the production capture backend.

name: Nothing reaches the screen until something has vouched for it
summary: A cover over the live/recorded seam is dropped only on evidence: a presented frame matching BOTH the handoff generation and the requested media timecode. Mismatches are discarded and the wait re-arms. A deadline's only reachable outcome is a held cover plus an honest retry — there is no path in the state machine from a deadline to a revealed state. The reveal is committed on a subsequent page paint with the evidence re-checked.
insight: A rule about what elapsed time may be evidence OF. A deadline is never admissible as evidence about pixels, but IS admissible as evidence about a correspondent's silence — one is a fact about a channel, the other a guess about a picture. Holding that line at four sites where a shortcut was locally tempting is the achievement.
field: The frame-presented callback is the documented tool; timecode matching is the first thing anyone doing frame-accurate seeking does; generation counters are textbook; the common industry pattern in players is a TIMEOUT-BACKED reveal that proceeds anyway rather than stall.
case_against: Three well-known parts bolted together; fail-closed is a cliche.
answer: Fail-closed here is the AGGRESSIVE choice — it accepts a permanently stuck interface to avoid a wrong frame, which is not what player frameworks do. The timer asymmetry is finer than 'fail closed' and I could not find it articulated in the field.
reverify_2026_08_19: client-web/lib/sim/** is byte-identical between 2d187e3 and origin/main. Structural claims all CONFIRMED. Corrections: single rAF not double; the auditor is test-only (zero production callers) but the guarantee is structural; the exhaustive test is 120 cases with one axis constant, one sampled, ordering not permuted. Still-live defect: frame callback without metadata falls back to the element clock but is labelled as the STRONG evidence kind, skipping every weaker-kind admissibility check. Untested.

name: What a package has proved about itself, and what survives a republish
summary: When a new immutable revision is derived from the active one, earned attestations are partitioned by what each is a fact ABOUT: package-level verdicts reset and must be re-earned; per-file facts are inherited only across bytes carried byte-for-byte; facts about files this publication rewrote are always re-derived; facts the derivation cannot answer fall back to the previous record and a confident negative is never manufactured. The whole set is projected onto the routing row from whichever revision the pointer lands on, so a rollback restores the matching attestations and the derived warm-up budget together.
insight: A reset is not neutral. In a system where downstream gates act on attestations, erasing a proved fact re-arms defensive behaviour and, if implemented as writing false, manufactures a claim nobody made. So inheritance is permitted only across provably identical bytes AT THE GRANULARITY AT WHICH THE FACT WAS EARNED, and 'I did not look' must never be written as 'the answer is no'.
field: Supply-chain practice binds an attestation to an artifact digest; guidance is explicit that an attestation cannot be matched without one and is immutable once published — so change the artifact and nothing carries over. Build systems solve the adjacent problem with finer-grained content-addressed caching. Tri-state capability detection where absence is its own case is a known runtime-capability pattern.
case_against: Each rule is individually forced by the problem statement; writing null rather than false is correct nullable-field hygiene.
answer: Each rule is obvious once you decide to have four rules. The non-obvious step is deciding a reset needs justifying at all — the digest-binding framing is so strong and correct in its own domain that adopting it wholesale is the natural move, and it causes a user-visible regression by manufacturing uncertainty.
caveat: The strongest consumer is unwired: the check that would refuse to PRESENT content certified broken (shared/src/sim/simFailurePolicy.ts:55-57 isPresentable) has zero production call sites. What is wired is narrower — unproven content is denied the aggressive activation path.

name: Consent bound to one exact plan
summary: The export plan is computed once, frozen, and hashed with a canonicalisation that REFUSES values it cannot represent faithfully rather than coercing them. The row is write-once — the running job is structurally forbidden to edit the plan, and what the run learns goes to a separate column. The user's agreement to a set of quality substitutions is a five-minute HMAC-signed token naming user, project, policy, plan fingerprint and expiry, with a named rejection set including plan_changed, which re-prompts rather than proceeding.
insight: The write-once record with a separate home for what the run learned: a plan that changes as it executes is not a snapshot, and the first question after a bad export is 'what were we actually asked to make?'.
field: Infrastructure automation has long supported saving a computed change plan and later applying it verbatim, explicitly so automation executes what a human reviewed, with interactive approval disabled when a saved plan is supplied. Short-lived signed capability tokens naming a subject, resource and expiry are the standard shape. Canonical serialisation for hashing is a solved, standardised problem.
case_against: Freeze, hash, sign. Each step is documented practice with mature tooling; the composition follows directly from the problem statement.
answer: Thin and not oversold. The only distinction is WHAT is consented to: the field's saved-plan pattern carries approval of changes to be MADE; here it carries acceptance of a DEGRADATION in the thing being made, which must not transfer to a different degradation.
listed_because: It is the substrate entry 1 stands on, and the write-once discipline is worth documenting.

name: An interface extracted from generated code, so the content beneath it can be swapped
summary: Before a package replacement is written, the platform-generated control program is read, every name it binds to is extracted (element ids, classes, label text, globals, function names), and each is resolved against the candidate bundle's markup, code AND styles together. Existence is asserted, not structure. Sections that could not be examined are reported unexaminable, never counted as passing. One broken section refuses the whole replace.
insight: Deriving a machine-checkable interface from generated code so a different artefact can be verified against it before swapping in — plus a deliberate false-negative bias, argued on the ground that a wrongly-allowed replace is caught seconds later by the owner's preview while a wrongly-blocked one makes the feature useless. Calibration criterion: a checker that fails the no-op replace is worse than no checker at all.
field: Consumer-driven contract testing — a consumer publishes the expectations it holds of a provider and the provider is verified against them before deployment — is mature with mainstream tooling, for exactly this purpose. Symbol-level compatibility checkers are standard in library ecosystems.
case_against: It is consumer-driven contract testing with the document tree standing in for an HTTP API; once you frame the generated program as the consumer, the design writes itself.
answer: The framing argument wins, which is why this is weak. What I would defend are engineering judgements rather than inventions: resolving across three languages because the interface is built at runtime, and calibrating against the identity replace.

name: Certification mints a runtime permission and its own fallback image
reason: Central claim REFUTED. The prior entry rested on one publish-time run producing four artefacts all keyed on ONE identity. Only the poster is config-keyed; the verdict is package-scoped; the budget is a worst case across cases; the bridge capability is not produced by the canary at all (different producer, different moment, different bytes). Surviving core is smaller but real: verdict re-derived from the report's own evidence and refused on disagreement; aborted runs forced to failure; vacuous success (zero steps) treated as its own failure; missing poster is a publish error. Four supporting weaknesses re-confirmed in current code: poster invalidation has one caller behind an optional script flag; both protocol versions recorded as 0 by the only production manifest builder; single-engine certification accepted while the pessimistic multi-engine merge has no production caller; the display-safety consumer is unwired. The PATTERN is this system's signature move and now has a better instance — see nov-2026-08-19-002.

name: Deterministic video export against a virtual clock
reason: Both prior findings stand against current code. The technique is the industry standard, matched part for part. And the reproducibility guarantee remains unestablished: startup virtual-frame burn still depends on real elapsed time; the compositor clock is still advanced by a real-time pump during page load, with a test asserting a six-frame slack band rather than equality; exactly one run-to-run byte-identity assertion exists, disabled by default, on a synthetic fixture, covering a non-production backend. Update in the owner's favour: nov-2026-08-19-001 pins one large environment-dependent term (which renderer did the work) as a verified property of the job.

name: Four-valued release audit where 'the checker broke' outranks 'the thing is broken'
reason: Infrastructure monitoring has carried a dedicated UNKNOWN state separate from CRITICAL since the 1990s, meaning exactly 'the check itself went wrong'. Unit-test frameworks have distinguished failure from error for as long. Deployment gating systems already treat a gate that could not evaluate as blocking. The one unmatched part — declaring coverage gaps inside the passing verdict — is a reporting choice, not a mechanism.

name: Proving a commit stands alone before making it (write-tree + archive + typecheck)
reason: CI on a clean checkout is the universal field answer; pre-commit tooling that hides unstaged changes so checks run against the staged state is mainstream. A faster local instance of a solved problem. Note: the script IS present in current origin/main at podcast-saas/deploy/scripts/verify-committed-tree.sh.

name: Anchoring overlays to content instead of to an absolute second
reason: Content-relative positioning is the decades-old standard answer — attached/linked clips in video editors, tempo-relative vs absolute positioning in audio workstations, anchored objects in word processors. The diagnosis was hard; the coordinate choice was not. The refusal to backfill (a migration that fixed every row would freeze every row's current mistake) is the best-argued data-migration reasoning in the repo but is a policy within the standard expand/contract dual-read pattern.

name: Reading a routing pointer late and treating a change as a conflict, not a branch
reason: Optimistic concurrency. Recognising that a derived verdict belongs to the transaction's read set is the definition of the isolation problem, not a new answer to it. The specific insight (re-routing would carry a stale compatibility verdict forward) is well argued and worth quoting.

name: Rewriting identity out of the bytes when a project is duplicated
reason: Rewriting embedded identifiers when cloning entities is standard in entity-cloning and data-subsetting tools. The hash calculus — recompute the hash that attests byte identity, deliberately leave stale the hash a third subsystem already derived paths from — is a subtle consequence of this schema rather than a general mechanism.

name: Independence proof inside the commit transaction, jsonb columns by schema reflection
reason: Verifying tenant isolation before committing a copy is standard multi-tenant discipline. 'The list is the defect' is a good implementation choice, not an invention.

name: 'Unknown is not success' in the artifact probe
reason: Validating an untrusted producer's output against the specification that requested it is what you are supposed to do. The reasoning (a missing frame count must fail, or the check rewards withholding it) is the purest statement of the system's stance and is worth quoting.

name: Exclusive slice allocation when recutting one synthesis into many clips
reason: Non-overlapping interval allocation is elementary. The asymmetric guards derived from a known directional bias in the vendor's timestamps are good engineering.

name: Auditing a vendor's alignment against an arithmetic identity of your own input
reason: Independently verifying a provider's alignment is documented practice in this field, and 'do not cache a degraded result' is known caching discipline. The cache-gating (use it now, refuse to make it permanent, so a rebuild self-heals) is the best part.

name: The sandbox argument set as the contract, and the artefact confinement stack
reason: Textbook container hardening, unusually well documented. Literal-stat-before-resolve, hard-link rejection, O_NOFOLLOW and descriptor-based validation are within known hardening practice.

name: The agent fleet's enforcement hook (allowlist inversion, option-stripping, heredoc body stripping)
reason: Allowlist-over-denylist is the canonical answer. The adversarial verification stage it supports is convention enforced by a language model, not by a program — no code reads or writes the verdict ledger described in the protocol.

name: Partition replacing overlapping classification filters; total order with the PK as tie-break
reason: Superb debugging (the query planner was effectively choosing which of two overlapping clips the viewer saw, which is why the bug was intermittent). 'Make your classification total and your ordering total' is basic.

name: Write/delete ordering derived from one perceptual invariant (prefer orphaned bytes)
reason: Both orderings correct, both conventional. Deriving them from one stated rule chosen on a perceptual criterion is above average, not novel.

name: Retirement rows, grace windows, GC retention floor of two, day-quantised token expiry
reason: Grace windows, retention floors and cache-key stability trades are standard. The floor-of-two reasoning (a floor of one collects exactly the set rollback chooses from, making rollback impossible while reporting success) and the day-quantised expiry are elegant and worth documenting.

name: LLM-pipeline structural guards: overlap demotion, monotonicity acceptance, constrained predicate accessor, permissive intermediate schemas
reason: Each is a good design choice within known practice. Note for the security fleet, not this dossier: the constrained accessor supplied to LLM-authored predicates includes a documented escape returning arbitrary globals, which defeats the accompanying denylist.

name: A reconciliation report that refuses to produce a verdict
reason: States plainly that the settling evidence lives in object storage and the database records none of it, emits candidates plus the exact key to check each against, names one outcome indeterminate, and notes that any column ending in 'to check' is an instruction to a human. Admirable. Not a mechanism.

name: Standard patterns wearing a local name
reason: Content-addressed cache keys; immutable versions with an atomic pointer flip; a private message channel to a sandboxed frame; generation/epoch tagging; tri-state capability flags; adaptive quality with hysteresis; rebuild-forcing vs live-applicable config partition; a page-wide priority lease; severity-classified deploy gates; a persisted resumable state machine; static classification of migration statements. All textbook, all correctly done.
